entities.name: Mul of Kent
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mul, a prince of the West Saxons and brother to King Cædwalla, briefly seized control of the Kingdom of Kent in 686 CE, reigning for approximately one tumultuous year until his violent death in 687 CE. His brief and brutal tenure represents a critical, albeit short-lived, expansion of West Saxon influence into the historically independent Kentish polity, marking a significant episode in the complex and often violent consolidation of early Anglo-Saxon England. His story is inextricably linked to the aggressive expansionist policies of his brother, Cædwalla, who sought to establish West Saxon hegemony over southern Britain in the late 7th century, bringing Kent under a foreign, West Saxon dominion for the first time in decades.

Mul's ascent to the Kentish throne was not through peaceful succession but by conquest, installed by his formidable brother Cædwalla, who had devastated Kent in 686 CE, likely in retaliation for the murder of his brother, the sub-king Cenfus. Mul's reign was characterized by instability and resentment among the Kentish populace, who viewed him as an imposed foreign ruler. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records that Mul ruled Kent for a year. His administration likely sought to extract resources and consolidate West Saxon authority, but faced deep-seated resistance from the native Kentish aristocracy and populace, who had long maintained their own dynastic lines and traditions.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mul's brief and violent reign significantly contributed to the instability of the Kingdom of Kent in the late 7th century and triggered a brutal retaliatory campaign by his brother, King Cædwalla, impacting the regional power balance in Anglo-Saxon England.
